I had seen such a list before at Mr. Slavko's, filled in in the same manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were unable to read any of the writing on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I could not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This document was not being shown at that distance to you for you to read and have a good look at what was on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I cannot affirm what they said, what was written on there, but I did not say that. All I said was the left-hand side was filled and the right-hand side was clean, and that one could see clearly because they were standing still and one could see it in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I suggest to you, Mr. Gutic, is that this simply is not true, that you did not see any list of names and you did not see Dusko Tadic discussing a document that was a list with the Deputy Camp Commander in front of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I still insist that Mr. Dusan Tadic and Mr. Slavko Puhalic were seen by myself in the situation I have described before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, any certificates that were, for example the certificate that you were asked about by Mr. Kay that allowed you to get out and look for milk, was that a document which just had a column down one side and the rest of the paper blank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the whole surface of that paper was filled. The central part of that certificate was written out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Other than the list which you saw in the possession of Slavko Puhalic which contained the names of Muslims who were to be called out of the camp, did you ever see any document in camp which just had a column written down one side and the rest of the paper blank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from time to time I went to the Red Cross office and there we collected bread or had contact with them, and I was present when men also applied for entry in a big, in a very thick notebook, because the camp administration had ordered that all men had to register so that they could be entered there, so that the record could be made. In that notebook they had lists with the first name and the surname of every individual who reported there. I think the father's name was entered as well, I believe, and the year of birth. Besides I saw similar lists when police came from Prijedor to the camp in a police van and they would hand over such a list to Slavko and Slavko would then take usually one or two soldiers, enter the camp and then look for people from that paper, from that sheet of paper, from that list, and men were taken away on the basis of such lists. I also remember an instance when one of the Balaban twins, who were Mr. Kuruzovic's body guards, came to ambulanta, it was towards the end of our stay there, and also brought a list of inmates and asked us, that is me and my colleague, to talk to people and talk them into signing those documents on emigration that we already talked about. So it was on various occasions that I saw such lists directly with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that the Serbian Red Cross was located in the building which housed the cinema, and also was later located across the street in the, in another building you referred to. Did the premises of the Serbian Red Cross move across the street before October 1st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Red Cross office was moved before 1st October. I would not know the date exactly, but no doubt before 4th August because a group of women was put there. Those who had been transferred from Omarska to Trnopolje, that is where they were put. Then in the course of August when they were taken away, when they left, inmates, that is male inmates, were put there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On the occasion when you saw Mr. Tadic and Deputy Commander Puhalic, were the premises of the Serbian Red Cross located in the cinema building, still located in the cinema building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have said I cannot remember clearly the date, but as Slavko was inside this was the time when the Red Cross was still in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just one matter arising, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Gutic, did Slavko Puhalic have an office in that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have said, Slavko Puhalic and the major were spending a large part of their time in those offices while in the camp, but Slavko Puhalic also had an office which was in another building beyond this large building, the former office of the local commune. There were some small offices and that is where Slavko also took inmates for interrogation when they interrogated, when he interrogated them and where some were beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is all I ask. Your Honour, I tender D28 as an Exhibit. I would like to make it an Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 28 will be admitted. Mr. Tieger any redirect, re-redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, casting your mind back to the surgery where you were and from which you observed these things, am I right in understanding your evidence to the effect that there was a wall and along that wall there were three windows, or was there one window which we saw in the photograph of the road and then the wall went round the corner and there were two other windows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was our surgery with one wall with three windows at a certain distance one from the another, and the road went at an angle of 90 degrees as against that wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies exactly what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Mr. Gutic, for the record may I know if you are qualified as a doctor now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Much to my regret I had three examinations left when the war broke out, so that my studies were discontinued. All these developments and the state that I am in and the new language that I have to learn, have prevented me from completing my studies. Moreover, my financial circumstances are very bad indeed as we have no possibility of obtaining some scholarship or any other kind of financial support. So I am waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gutic, would you estimate for me by looking in this courtroom how far Mr. Tadic was away from you when you saw this list about which you testified, from where you are to either where I am or where the table is or where the Prosecutor's table is? Give me a benchmark so that I can better understand this distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the far right corner of this courtroom we see a gentleman in uniform and a little bit further away, that is another metre which is slightly over a yard further away, that is roughly the distance.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: My second question relates to your testimony about the consequences that Muslim women face in a patriarchal society. You testified that Muslim women in a patriarchal society suffer certain consequences when they are raped. Would you explain that further for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that Bosnian Muslims, especially in a rural environment, are rather patriarchal, they are brought up very conservatively, their father has the predominant role and the girls are brought up very strictly. Moreover, I do not say this is a rule, that need not be so, but looking at them, girls usually marry at a rather early age, that is around 19, and I have to put it that way. It was [sic] desirable for them to have slept or rather have had contact with another man. Those who did for various other reasons were second-rate persons of a second-rate category. So that rape which happens very, very seldom with us, I know of only one case which is an even worse, an even more terrible incident, such persons girls who were raped, not only because of the psychological trauma that they go through, but because they become outcasts in their environment, their environment discarded them and they would cease to be, if I may say so, attractive for marriage or to become a member of a family. Their family plays an important role, if one might say, the frame of mind of Bosnian Muslims, a family with two or three children, the family has a predominant role. That is I believe an additional factor which is a further strain on those girls, as compared with some girls who were raped outside that area or perhaps in an urban environment and such like. Moreover, they are faced with a mental conflict, that is the manner of their up bringing, very strict education and then all the circumstances of all that happens afterwards.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: The translation said "desirable". I gather that the witness meant "not desirable". Did you see that, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I think it was quite clear in the context. It was a translation problem.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are there additional questions, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Gutic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gutic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming. We will adjourn for one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (2.45 p.m.) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger? Cross-examination -- no, we finished with Mr. Gutic real quickly. Would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Mr. Sefik Kesic. MR. SEFIK KESIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you take that oath that has been given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sefik, Kesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How old are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You are a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you raised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First years in Kamicani and four years in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At Rade Kondic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what years did you serve?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were your duties in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the engineering units and I was a Corporal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After service in the JNA, did you work in Slovenia and Croatia in construction and did you also attend courses to become a driver and work as a driver?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you still maintain your home in Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that where your home was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often would you come home during the time you worked in Slovenia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first, twice or once, once or twice a month, and later when I got a car, I had a car, then more frequently, almost every weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the two years before the war, did you return home to the Kozarac/Kamicani area after your wife died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in Kamicani and Kozarac until the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Kozarac the main or primary shopping and cafe area for the people of Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that where you went for food, supplies, documents and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you in Kozarac frequently, in particular, during the two years which preceded the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost every week, at least once.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you friends or acquaintances with Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long have you known who he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, going back five, six years, for five or six years.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it five or six years before the war when you became aware that this particular person was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before that time were you familiar with him simply as a resident of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you learn who Mr. Tadic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When passing through Kozarac in the street since this was a man, so to speak, better known. He was a trainer of a club that I never visited. He was greeted by the inhabitants, the youth and the children, so that I heard that they greet him with "Hello, Dule", "Hello, Dusko", "Hello, Tadic". The older would greet him, "Hello Tadic", so that I knew that it was this Dusan Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you continue to see him in Kozarac after the time you learned what his name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, I want to direct your attention to the beginning of the conflict, the actual military attack in Kozarac. Were you at home when the attack on Kozarac began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who were you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there with my children and my parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were your children's ages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a small daughter of four. I had two male children. One was born in '78 and the other was born in '80.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the attack began, did you and your family flee to the forest for shelter along with many others from your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you think at that time that you would be leaving your homes for a long period of time or for good?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you imagine at that point would happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought, like everybody else, that it was going to be several days of shooting and that we would all come back to our homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From the area of the forest, were you able to see what was happening to your village and to your homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was happening? What could you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw that the military and tanks, a couple of tanks, let us say two tanks there were, they started at the edge of the village from Forici to set houses on fire, to destroy houses and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, how many nights did you and your family spend in the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On the fourth day of the attack, did you and your family move from the forest and go to Kozarac for the purpose of surrendering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About how large was the group that you went with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the beginning, it was a group of about 300 persons, but coming towards Kozarac it was growing as the people from other shelters were joining in this column.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you reached the square in Kozarac, the point where the old road meets Marsala Tita, were men told at that point to march ahead of the women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my estimate, there was about 1,000 at the time when we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you got there, that is, to that area where the old road meets Marsala Tita, were men at that point told to separate from the women and march ahead of the women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what direction were you told by Serbian forces to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To go towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the area of Susici, near the Limenka bus stop, were men separated from the women and children and told to board buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you attempt to plead with or speak with a Serbian soldier or soldiers in order to be allowed to stay with your children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you permitted to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was your father also in the group of men that were marching ahead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How old was he?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he go with the group of women and children or did he go with the group of men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the men, he went.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you and your children then board a bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Trnopolje camp, first of all, were there people already there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you estimate how many people were already at Trnopolje camp when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 1,000, 1500. I could not estimate exactly because there were some in the school, but outside were about 1,000 to 1500 people.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the transcript has stopped, Miss Featherstone tells me. We are not seeing it on our monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour, the same situation here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is it still not operative? Is it still not on the monitor? Let us see. Are we operating now? I see the words "Presiding Judge" several times but that is all -- yes, very good. OK. Mr. Tieger, you need to repeat, I suppose, a couple of questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, there were a couple of questions that were not picked up on the transcript so I will ask those again. After you and your children boarded the bus, were you then taken to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there a large number of people already gathered there when you arrived ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- in various portions of the camp and the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did people continue to arrive after you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was food provided for the prisoners of Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the beginning of the operation of the camp, was it possible for some people who had relatives in the nearby area to receive permission to stay with those relatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After three or four days in the camp, did you and your children receive permission to stay with an uncle in Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many refugees were in Sivci at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could not estimate because all the houses were full, but there were certainly, in my estimate, 2,000 to 2500.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many refugees were in your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were about 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After a period of time in Sivci was there a cleansing of the men in Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About how long after you got to your uncle's house was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After 14 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did that cleansing begin? What did you first see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since my uncle's house is at the end of the village starting from the camp, we were in the houses and the soldiers came with one tank. They ordered that all men come out of the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the soldiers armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had firearms, automatic rifles, rifles and hand guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What time was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was afternoon, around 1 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you try to tell these soldiers, as you had done at Limenka, that your wife was dead and that your children only had you to help them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did they say this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That soldier whom I asked, he thought and asked another soldier next to him and he said, "No way", that I had to go on the road, that I had to -- that I had to start down the road, that I could not stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there groups of Muslim men running down the road at this point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you and the others from the house form a group or join another group running down the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened as you began running down the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We ran down the road one after the other, and they ordered us to lie down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you did lie down, what could you see and hear happening around you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were -- there was beating, there were screams. People were being beaten and there was blood on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you eventually collected with others in the courtyard of a large house farther down the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After a short time there, were you ordered to board buses which had arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know how many buses arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I was not in the last bus I could not count but, in my estimate, there were about six to seven buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you boarded the bus, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us past the Trnopolje camp to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Keraterm camp were guards waiting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened to the prisoners as they got off the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were beaten by these soldiers, these guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what part of Keraterm camp were you then held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in room 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we have Exhibit 201 for just a moment? Sir, do you recognise what is shown in that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the Keraterm camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May 201 be placed for a moment on the Elmo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, can you point out on that photograph where room 2 was or where the area where you were held was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Please do so with the pointer on the desk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. How long were you held at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was about 20 to 25 days there. I could not -- I cannot remember the exact number of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that were you transferred to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you transferred with the main group of prisoners from Omarska camp to Manjaca thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, what was the nationality of the prisoners in Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What percentage, a higher percentage of one group than the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were more Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were the general conditions in Keraterm like during the time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conditions were dreadful. We were hungry. We were cramped. We were almost on top of one another. There were no conditions so that one could wash one's face or brush the teeth or anything at least once, not to mention twice, a day. The hygiene was non-existent. There was only one toilet that we all used and the stench was terrible because nobody cleaned it. But hunger, hunger was the worst. One ate once a day and one would be given something that they called "soup", but it looked more like water than like soup, and a small piece of bread and that was all. The vessels that we ate from were never washed, but three or four of us would eat from the same container that was never washed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did people become ill with diseases such as disentery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was medical care provided for such people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, were there beatings and killings in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners called from the rooms and taken out and beaten or tortured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often would this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened almost every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would some of the prisoners return from being called out with various kinds of injuries from the beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Some less, some more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did some of the prisoners die from the injuries they received during these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did some of the prisoners who were called out simply disappear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, shortly after your arrival in Keraterm, were you among a group of prisoners who were called out of the room and beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall exactly how long this was after you arrived in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly I would not know the number of days, but it was during the first 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did this happen during the day or at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you know, about what time of night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was not late into the night. It could have been two or three hours after dusk, after the sun set. So it was the evening, around 9 o'clock perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you in the room before you were called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was near the entrance, near the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before you were called out, in what position were you -- standing, sitting, lying down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Around the time you mentioned, did a group of soldiers or uniformed people come into the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When they came in, did you and the other prisoners react in some way? Did you change positions in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We endeavoured to be as small as possible, to be the least conspicuous as possible and we tried to shrink.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there a light inside the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the group came into the room, did one of them say anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said something like, "Does anybody want to return", those soldiers or him personally, all that we were, would anybody like to pay back to him or other soldiers for all the beatings everything that happened, so if anybody wanted to beat back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any of the prisoners volunteer to do that at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were various comments that we were cowards, that we were no combatants, and then, well, if there is, he said, "Well, 10 of you may come out if you -- feel free, nothing will happen to them now, nothing will happen to them later".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any of the prisoners respond to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You and the others just continued to try to make yourself as invisible as possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then he said, "Then I will pick out myself, if you do not want to come out yourselves".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At that point were people picked out or did people leave at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he pick out particular people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were the people who left the room selected to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said something like, "First, you two, from you two the first 10 come out".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know from your position in the room or from glancing around that you were among the first 10 in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you and the others leave the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stood up, one after the other, and came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you got outside of the room, did you form a group or did you walk forward in a line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We walked one after the other in a line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there light outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was light. It came from a car which had its lights on. There was nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you and the other prisoners formed a line outside of room 2, did you see whether there were guards or soldiers around you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened after you and the others were lined up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then one walked from one to the other, asking what was his name, where he came from, whether he had any weapons, and hitting him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that done one prisoner at a time, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately, where were you in the line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was somewhere in the middle. Yes, I was somewhere in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened when the person who was going from prisoner to prisoner asking questions and beating them reached you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me what my name was, where I came from, whether I had any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At that point were you supposed to look down at the ground or were you supposed to look at the person asking you the questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You had to look at him, to look up at his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise who that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After he asked you your name, where you came from and whether you had weapons, first of all, what did you answer when he asked whether you had weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I did not have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he say anything in response to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, "You all say that you did not have any weapons, that you don't have any weapons".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me, and struck me at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you struck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, around the stomach, a little bit higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened to you after you were struck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was gasping for air. I remained breathless and I squatted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You squatted on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I went down on to my knees on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you struck anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment, no, or I do not remember well, but later when we returned, on my upper lip I had -- from inside it was slightly injured, there was a little blood, but I paid no attention to that and that blow if I was hit indeed do not remember at all. I did not consider it a blow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you finally able to rise from that squatting position on your own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic continue to go down the line of prisoners to the ones who had not yet been beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he beat them as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did some of the other guards or soldiers who were around the group of prisoners also participate in the beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After all the prisoners had been beaten, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken back to the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall what Dusko Tadic was wearing on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a camouflage multi-coloured uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, you mentioned that prisoners were regularly beaten in Keraterm. Was there a group or groups of persons from outside the camp who would come regularly to call prisoners out and beat them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there some persons who came with these groups more frequently to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The most frequent visitor was Zoran Zigic called "Ziga" and Duca. I know his nickname name "Duca", I do not know either his first name or his surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As a result of the incident which you described during which you were beaten by Dusko Tadic, did you regard him as part of the group or groups that came virtually every day or night to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, I noted that in your statement to the Tribunal investigator it said that you saw Tadic more or less every day in Keraterm. Did you mean by that that you saw Dusko Tadic more or less every day in Keraterm with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see him every day with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Other than the occasion you have just described for us, did you ever see Dusko Tadic in Keraterm with your own eyes in such a way that you could be certain it was him as you were on that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But you regarded him as part of the groups that came more or less every day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, do you see Dusko Tadic in court here today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you point him out, please, and tell us what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He has a jacket and a tie, a shirt, blue, and so .....

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect the identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect that the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is all I have, your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This occasion that you have described as having been beaten by Dusko Tadic, Mr. Kesic, happened during the night time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are uncertain of the date. You cannot help us with when this occurred, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the occasion that you describe, how many guards or soldiers were involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about five or six of them, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had been in room 2 of Keraterm camp at this time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that the first room in Keraterm that you were placed in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On any occasion before this, had you been taken out of your room and beaten by guards or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you been interrogated at Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you beaten during that interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long after this incident did you remain in Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 15 days or so, perhaps two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you receive any beatings in that period afterwards that you were in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Zigic at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see the man that you called Duca at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were taken out of room 2 on the occasion you say that Dusko Tadic beats you, did you know why you and other prisoners were being taken from that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it was not a case that you were selected for any particular reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was a random taking of you and others from that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had been positioned by the door of that room as your spot in the room for the previous 10 days, had you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you the first to be taken out of the room or the last or in the middle? Can you tell me about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was somewhere in the middle, neither the first nor the last.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were all this group of 10 near that door, in the area that you were in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was no light inside the room, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had the door to that room been shut beforehand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But did a guard or a soldier come to the door of the room and select you and the others, tell you to come out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you got out of the room, were you put in a line or were you just standing around as a group of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They lined us up in a column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I can put the question this way, had your interrogation by someone in the camp taken place before this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you been questioned about arms or weapons during your detention in Keraterm before this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had other people, do you know, in that room No. 2 where you were held been questioned and interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As part of their questioning, do you know if they had been questioned about things such as weapons or arms or whether they were involved in paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had any of that group that you were in, the 10 men taken from room No. 2, previously been questioned or interrogated, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, can you remember any of the other names of the people in that group of 10 from room No. 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a relative of mine, Sivac Dudo. I remember him. He was next to me. I cannot remember others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know any of the other guards or soldiers who were part of that group who were beating you outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In being asked these questions, whether you had weapons or arms, was it a proper questioning? Were you expected to answer what was being asked of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did anyone reply to this questioning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you answer to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I answered that I did not have any kind of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was a random group taken from that room who were being asked these questions. You were not a particular group of 10 men who had anything in common, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The lighting outside this room, you said, came from a vehicle. Where was that parked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was parked in front of this dormitory of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where were the lights shining?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were directed towards the camp, towards our dormitory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I can take it, can I, from the questioning by the Prosecution that you have made allegations that Dusko Tadic had assaulted you on other occasions about which you were not sure that it was him, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you tell the Prosecution that you were not sure about those other occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the occasion of the second interrogation or the third, then I said I was not sure that I saw him every time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I might ask you what the date was, if you can remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date, but it was after -- about five, six days after the first case was that second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long ago, can you tell me in terms of weeks or months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not understand the whole question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not know the dates of your interviews, you see. How long ago would that have been that you told them that you were not certain about the other things you had said? How long ago from today's date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some four or five months ago, approximately, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So what it comes to is this, that you are saying you are certain about this one occasion and this happened some 10 days after you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic was not a man that you knew well, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He was not a man you drunk with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or eaten with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or socialised with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The time when you say you saw him, this was at night time when the light was coming from a vehicle that was shining towards that dormitory where you and the others were lined up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Miso Danicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see, what I suggest to you is that you are mistaken about that man who attacked you being Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As you have made allegations before that you were uncertain about, is this something as well that really you are uncertain about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you still making this allegation because of the need to stand by something in accusing Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is my duty to say what I know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just one question, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, was there sufficient light the night you were beaten to recognise that the man right in front of you asking you questions was Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, when you were lined up, were you in a line parallel to the building that we have seen in the photograph with your backs to the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were turned with our backs to the building as we came out of the building, so we lined up in front of it.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That means you were facing the lights of the motor car, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Whoever beat you would have had his back to the motor car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How would he have been positioned then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came out, and I forgot to say that, I apologise, out of the dormitory we were standing facing the light. Then we all turned to the left, to the left, so that the light was coming from the right.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So it was not a question of each one of you turning, but the whole line pivoted, did it, round to a position right angles to the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, do you recall the date that you went to Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was around June 15th.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Let us see. You were taken to Trnopolje four days after the attack at Kozarac, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You stayed there for three or four days, is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Then you went to Sivci, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Then after about 14 days after being in Sivci you were taken to Keraterm, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, if I could see Exhibit 201 again? May that be placed on the Elmo?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, if you could just show us using the pointer how the row of prisoners was lined up after you left room 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph] We were lined up like this, straight, and then we turned this way, pivoting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: That does not tell me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Sir, I think you indicated that the prisoners left room 2 one by one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Walking out one behind the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you walked out, therefore, with your backs to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then at some point did the group stop as it proceeded out from the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that the approximate position then of the row of prisoners during the time you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the group came out from the room one by one, walked a certain distance and then basically stopped and turned and then that was the position in which the beating occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know if that ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I have nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One more question, Mr. Kesic. Was the line of prisoners between the dormitory and where the car was parked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you show us on Exhibit 201 approximately where that vehicle was parked with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. [The witness indicated on the photograph]. It was around here, approximately. There was a kiosk where those guards -- there was a kiosk where those guards were like hid from the rain, and the car was here, here around.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay? Additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Mr. Kesic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: May it please your Honour, I call Adil Jakupovic. ADIL JAKUPOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Jakupovic, would you please take the oath that is being given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is your full name Adil Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When were you born, Mr. Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 23rd November '41.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you born in the village of Jakupovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately, how far is that from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about six kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you start your primary school in Jakupovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then did you continue in Kozarac, in the Kozarac primary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do some of your secondary school in Kozarac before going to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went for training to a store and then to a school in Banja Luka because one had to undergo training first and then continue the schooling.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you live in the Kozarac area right up until the beginning of the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you work as a manager of a warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for about 12 or 13 years I worked in some two or three shops, and then the rest of the time I worked in the warehouse of a wholesale company in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do your military service in 1967 through to 1968?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you attend your military service in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you Muslim? Is Muslim your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said that you were a manager of a warehouse. How long before the attack on Kozarac did you work in that position, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for some six or seven days, something like that. Then they forbid us to go to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was that people who were non-Serb were forbidden to go to work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the attack on Kozarac occur on 24th May 1992 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you taking shelter in a basement of a neighbour's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the shelling, I was sitting with my neighbour in front of his house and we were talking that this might happen, and after several minutes the first shell fell and then we ran down under his staircase. We stayed there, I do not know, there were countless shells which fell and broke a window on his house. Then we moved on to basement where it was slightly safer. When it stopped for a while, I rushed out to see what was happening to my family, whether they were all right, because they were to be with a neighbour who had a concrete cellar. I think it was three houses away from mine. His name was Namik Majic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But subsequently did you then flee into the woods surrounding Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you stay in these woods for a period of approximately four days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I had a summer cottage in the woods on the top, at the end of the inhabited area, some 600 metres of altitude. My son and daughter and my wife left with a neighbour in a car in the direction of that summer cottage, and my elder son and I started through Kozarac. My son moved faster and he left. I did not see him. Later on, I learned that he had turned left in the woods and I went towards the village of Brdjani up there towards my summer cottage. I followed the road for a while and then I continued through the forest, as the road which took us by the mountaineer's lodge was under constant fire, so there was no way. When I was coming down every 20 or 30 centimetres there was a shell, so I reached the summer cottage and I did not find my family there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you subsequently meet up with your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Subsequently, when I saw they were not there, I returned to look for them. I assumed that I ought to find them, whether alive or dead, along the way which they were to follow. I passed along that road and I did not find them, so I thought they must have been dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But subsequently you did find them, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that I did find them in a ditch, under a big tree, under a bush. I found them and we went to the other side of the forest because I knew the road which was shelled less and we reached the summer cottage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I asked you earlier, after four days you then came back down into Kozarac because other people were doing that, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One night we came down from the forest to a village called Vidovici above Kozarac, and we spent that day there and the night, and the next day we were told that we all had to come down because they were about to shell that area within about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you came down into Kozarac, did you and members of your family meet someone there that you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came down by car and my family with two neighbours, and we came down to the Prijedor/Banja Luka road, and there were lots of military there, lots of people, waiting for buses or what do I know? Meanwhile, a soldier came up to me and asked me if I was Adila Jakupovic and I said, "Yes". He said, "Come over here, Zoran Karlica wants to see you". This was a friend of mine, a mountaineer, with whom I had spent a lot of time mountaineering and he worked in a mountaineers's club, and he was a reserve officer of the Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He was a Serb himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did Zoran Karlica then do with you and your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said he would take us over, he would transfer us to Prijedor, and with me, Sead Kusuran, my neighbour, and his mother came along with me. He asked, "Do you have to go somewhere?" He perhaps thought of taking us somewhere and then said, suggested that he take us to his mother-in-law who lived in Prijedor and he drove us there and left us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then stay in Prijedor city itself, in two locations in that city, for a period of four months from this date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you lived in Kozarac, what part of Kozarac did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in Titova Street, somewhere around the centre, No. 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might the witness please be shown Exhibit 220? Mr. Jakupovic, I would ask you, please, to just look at that plan for a moment and familiarise yourself with it. Then I am going to ask that it be put on the overhead projector and I will get you to point for me at where your house was located, approximately. OK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I did ask that we put that on an overhead projector and it will now come up on the television screen in front of you. Can I ask you to point to it on the machine there, not on the computer, with a pointer, if you can, point to where your house was? You need to hold it very steady when you put it on there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan] My house was here, more or less, here in this corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the accused in these proceedings, Mr. Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometime in '69 I bought this lot and started building the house there and Dusko Tadic's house -- and there was one man between us. He together with me bought that lot, but I began to build my house before him and that is when I met his father I knew well. I mean, as I was building the house, Dusko Tadic was a child then, but I mean I used to see his brothers across this boundary. Then, later on over the years, of course, I came to know him quite well, although considering that he must be some 20 years younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The house that Dusko Tadic lived in was one house away from your house, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who owned the house in the middle, between your house and Dusko Tadic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sulejman Mujagic's house, we had bought that plot of land together and then reached an understanding and started building our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask, please, that the witness be shown this photograph. There are extra copies made for your Honours, an enlarged version of it. Perhaps it could be marked Exhibit 299? Just look at that photograph, if you would, for me, please, Mr. Jakupovic? Can you tell me if you recognise what you see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my house -- former.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I ask that that photograph be placed on the overhead projector. Perhaps it could be blown up to its full size? Mr. Jakupovic, using the pointer for me again, please, on the photograph itself would you please point to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just hold the photograph still, please. Point to it again for me, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Right. Can you point to the house of Sulejman Mujagic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you point to the house where Dusko Tadic lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender that photograph, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 299 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown this photograph and it be given the number 300?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, I am having a problem with this Exhibit 299, identifying Mr. Tadic's house. The witness says it is ----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will ask the witness to do it again.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just so that when we go back and try to look at this, we will know what we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: By all means. Before the witness is given that photograph, could you please give the witness back Exhibit 299 and can it be placed on the overhead projector? Mr. Jakupovic, I would ask you, please, with the pointer to hold the pointer very steady on the house that you say Dusko Tadic lived in, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just hold it in place. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now might the witness be shown 300? Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is it a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the photograph of the Tadics' house and this part is his coffee bar. This part here was residential. I think that one of the brothers had opened their storage room.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK. I will ask you some questions about that. Might it be placed on the overhead projector, please? Can you point to the part of the house which you said was his cafe bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph]. These were the business premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just hold it steady there. Do you know in what part of that building Dusko Tadic himself lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the entrance and this is part of the old house, and there he lived in this part of the old house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this house sort of built in one stage and then subsequently added to, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This part here that you can see was a smaller house. It existed when I came to the primary school and then it was added and built up, I do not know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you, if you can -- you may not be able to -- point to the parts that were added to subsequently after the main building, the first building, went in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This here part with the restaurant, this is part of the old house, this part here, although this was added, there was one room and perhaps one door. Here, I believe there were three rooms here. I do not remember any more. This did not exist and the roof was turned like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Jakupovic, if you are to help us, you will need to hold the pointer in one spot and leave it there otherwise it is too quick and we do not see what you are pointing to. Do you know the name of the cafe bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The coffee bar was called Nipon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there a sign saying "Nipon cafe bar"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was that sign located, are you able to point to that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph]. I think it was here above the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I tender that photo. 300?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 300, is it ----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: 300, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- 300 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Jakupovic, was your family and the Tadic family close and did you socialise with each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My wife was friends with his wife and mother, and I saw his father quite often, we thought him one of exemplary citizens there. He was a man who fought in the last war since '41 and he knew a lot, and I liked talking to him. He told us stories about the last war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know Dusko Tadic's brothers and the other members of the family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know his wife's family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the time that you saw Dusko Tadic in Kozarac, did you know him to have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes he had a beard, sometimes he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So, it was a case of growing it and then shaving it off and then growing it back again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was fashionable at a certain time, not everybody had a beard, but what do I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from Mr. Tadic being involved in his cafe bar, did you know what other interests he had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was into karate in the school, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he coach karate, so far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, he instructed young people, boys, lads -- I do not know much about that -- I guess from small children to grown ups.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether Dusko Tadic had any interest in politics at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
